<module id="div_8bit">
    <description>Implements a simplified radix-2 divider for 8-bit signed or unsigned integers. Supports both signed and unsigned division operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">The clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst">The reset signal to initialize or reset the module.</input>
        <input id="sign">Indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0).</input>
        <input id="dividend" width_description="[7:0]">The 8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division.</input>
        <input id="divisor" width_description="[7:0]">The 8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division.</input>
        <input id="opn_valid">A 1-bit input signal indicating the presence of a valid operation request.</input>
        <input id="res_ready">A 1-bit input signal indicating that the 16-bit output result has already been acknowledged.</input>
        <output id="res_valid">A 1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready.</output>
        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">The 16-bit output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="DIVIDE">1'b0</parameter>
        <parameter id="REMAINDER">1'b1</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="res_valid_reg" init_value="1'b0">Register to hold the result validity status.</reg>
        <reg id="start_cnt" init_value="1'b0">Register to indicate the start of the division process.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt" init_value="1'b0">Register to keep track of the current iteration count during division.</reg>
        <reg id="neg_divisor" width_description="[7:0]" init_value="8'h00">Register to store the negative value of the divisor.</reg>
        <reg id="dividend_abs" width_description="[7:0]" init_value="8'h00">Register to store the absolute value of the dividend.</reg>
        <reg id="divisor_abs" width_description="[7:0]" init_value="8'h00">Register to store the absolute value of the divisor.</reg>
        <reg id="SR" width_description="[15:0]" init_value="16'h0000">Shift register to store the intermediate results during division.</reg>
        <always_comb>
            // Update the result validity status based on the reset signal, counter, and result consumption
            if(rst == 1'b1 || cnt[7] == 1'b1 && res_valid_reg == 1'b1)begin
                res_valid_reg = 1'b0;
            end else if(cnt == 8'd8 && res_valid_reg != 1'b1)begin
                res_valid_reg = 1'b1;
            end else if(res_valid_reg == 1'b1 && res_ready == 1'b1)begin
                res_valid_reg = 1'b0;
            end else begin
                res_valid_reg = res_valid_reg;
            end
        </end
        <always @(posedge clk) begin
            // Perform division operation when opn_valid is high and res_valid is low
            if(opn_valid == 1'b1 && res_valid_reg == 1'b0)begin
                // Save the dividend and divisor values
                dividend_abs <= dividend;
                divisor_abs <= divisor;
                
                // Initialize the shift register SR with the absolute value of the dividend shifted left by one bit
                SR <= {dividend_abs, 1'b0};
                
                // Set the negative divisor value
                neg_divisor <= ~divisor_abs + 1'b1;
                
                // Reset the counter cnt and start_cnt
                cnt <= 1'b0;
                start_cnt <= 1'b1;
            end
            
            // Division process
            if(start_cnt == 1'b1)begin
                // Check if the counter cnt has reached the most significant bit (MSB)
                if(cnt[7] == 1'b1)begin
                    // Reset the counter cnt and start_cnt
                    cnt <= 1'b0;
                    start_cnt <= 1'b0;
                    
                    // Update the shift register SR with the final remainder and quotient
                    SR <= {SR[14:0], 1'b0} | ({SR[14:0], 1'b0} >> 1);
                end else begin
                    // Increment the counter cnt
                    cnt <= cnt + 1'b1;
                    
                    // Perform subtraction operation
                    case(SR[15:8])
                        8'hFF: begin
                            SR[15:8] <= SR[15:8] + neg_divisor;
                        end
                        default: begin
                            SR[15:8] <= SR[15:8];
                        end
                    endcase
                    
                    // Multiplexer selection based on the carry-out
                    case({SR[15], SR[15]})
                        2'b00: begin
                            SR[15:8] <= SR[15:8];
                        end
                        2'b01: begin
                            SR[15:8] <= SR[15:8] + neg_divisor;
                        end
                        2'b10: begin
                            SR[15:8] <= SR[15:8] + neg_divisor;
                        end
                        2'b11: begin
                            SR[15:8] <= SR[15:8];
                        end
                    endcase
                    
                    // Shift the shift register SR left by one bit
                    SR <= {SR[14:0], 1'b0};
                end
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        When opn_valid is high and res_valid is low, save the inputs dividend and divisor.
        Initialize the shift register SR with the absolute value of the dividend shifted left by one bit.
        Set NEG_DIVISOR to the negated absolute value of the divisor.
        Set the counter cnt to 1 and start_cnt to 1 to begin the division process.
        
        If start_cnt is high, perform the division process:
        If the counter cnt reaches 8 (most significant bit of cnt is set), the division is complete:
        Clear cnt and start_cnt.
        Update the shift register SR with the final remainder and quotient.
        Otherwise, increment the counter cnt and update the shift register SR based on the subtraction result:
        Compute the subtraction of NEG_DIVISOR.
        Use a multiplexer to select the appropriate result based on the carry-out.
        Update SR by shifting left and inserting the carry-out.
        
        Manage res_valid based on the reset signal, counter, and whether the result has been consumed.
    </implementation>
</module>
